words.meaning: reducing the value, strength, or ownership share of something
words.example: The founders rejected the financing offer because it would be too dilutive for early shareholders.

words.meaning: to reduce the likelihood or impact of a potential problem
words.example: We can derisk the migration by moving one customer segment at a time.

words.meaning: to gradually discontinue a product, service, or policy
words.example: The company will sunset the legacy dashboard after every client moves to the new version.

words.meaning: to involve something as a necessary part or consequence
words.example: Expanding into Europe will entail hiring local legal and support teams.

words.meaning: to pay out money from a fund or account
words.example: Finance will disburse the grant money once the contracts are signed.

phrases.meaning: to abandon a plan or take emergency action before things get worse
phrases.example: If error rates keep climbing, we should pull the ripcord and roll back the release.

phrases.meaning: to gain a clear understanding of or accurately locate something
phrases.example: We interviewed several customers to get a bead on why renewals were slipping.

phrases.meaning: to avoid helping someone by repeatedly delaying or redirecting them
phrases.example: The airline gave me the runaround when I asked for a refund.

phrases.meaning: to gain an early advantage by acting before others
phrases.example: We ordered the materials early to get the jump on the holiday rush.

phrases.meaning: to do much of the difficult work for a person, group, or cause
phrases.example: Maya carried the water for the team while two coworkers were out sick.
